contract_tests: tests/test_merge_config_regression.py::test_returns_all_keys_from_base_and_overrides asserts merge_config({"a": 1}, {"a": 2, "b": 3}) == {"a": 2, "b": 3} and merge_config({}, {}) == {} (keys from both inputs, simple override preserved).

tests/test_merge_config_regression.py::test_recursive_merge_of_nested_mappings asserts merge_config({"a": {"x": 1, "y": 2}}, {"a": {"y": 3, "z": 4}}) == {"a": {"x": 1, "y": 3, "z": 4}} (recursive merge, override wins at leaf, base-only and override-only keys preserved).
tests/test_merge_config_regression.py::test_lists_are_replaced_not_concatenated asserts merge_config({"a": [1, 2]}, {"a": [3]}) == {"a": [3]} and result type is list.
tests/test_merge_config_regression.py::test_does_not_mutate_inputs asserts base and overrides dicts are unchanged (== original literals) after the call.

tests/test_merge_config_regression.py::test_result_is_independent_of_inputs asserts mutating result nested objects does not affect base/overrides, and mutating base/overrides after the call does not affect the previously returned result.
tests/test_merge_config_regression.py::test_no_shared_nested_objects asserts result nested dict/list objects are not identical (is not) to those in base or overrides.

edits.old:
def merge_config(defaults, overrides):
    result = dict(defaults)
    result.update(overrides)
    return result

patches.rationale: Rewrite merge_config to recursively merge nested mappings, replace lists wholesale, and return fully independent data (deep-copied leaves) without mutating or aliasing either input. Add a new regression test file covering all acceptance contracts.
